🏛️ On Monday, an unelected House starts deciding how you vote.

The Representation of the People Bill — lowering the voting age to 16, rewriting donation rules, expanding Electoral Commission powers — reaches the House of Lords.

📅 52 people were given seats in that chamber this year alone:
• 26 announced on 12 May (former hereditary peers handed life peerages)
• 26 more announced on 16 July — four days before Keir Starmer left office

⚖️ Credit where it's due: scrapping hereditary peers was a real reform. But 26 of them were converted to life peers and sent straight back in. The principle was retired; the people were retained.

🗳️ Swapping an accident of birth for a favour from the Prime Minister isn't democracy. It's the same problem in a different suit.
